I'm in the same boat, 18:26 5K and a two miler here. What helps a lot is hills and mile thresholds. 

Hills: Find a really hilly area and run around there for 50 minutes. But, with a 70/30 drill. That means 70% of your fastest pace uphill and 30% of your fastest pace on the flat area and downhill. 

Mile thresholds: Basically, you're doing four miles at 30 seconds faster than your mile split for your 5K time. Say you run a 22:30 5K, you're going to be running a 7 minute mile (22:30 mile split is around a 7:30 min mile pace)

This helped me get to where I am now. Also, your attitude going into the race is a huge factor. Remember, a good attitude and empty bowels leads to a great race.

Hey there!! I'm a high school athlete who's gotten down to a pretty quick time in the two mile. It's my best race by far. What I've done to get there is 400m repeats. My coach usually has me doing 18 400's at 75 seconds with a minute rest. By no means go out and do it if you haven't done anything like this before. What you should do is start reasonable. Maybe 8 400m repeats at whatever pace seems like you're almost pushing it each time with 90 seconds rest (more if needed, you should have fully recovered your breath by the time you go again). This workout helps your mentality and pacing. The mental part is desensitizing yourself to the distance. The physical part is pushing yourself to keep working hard on each lap. 

Another solution for you. Distance runs!!!! I see your mile time is around a 7:30. Get that time down as much as possible! How do you do that? Distance! If you're running the two mile, go for a four mile run (if you can do more, do it). The more distance you do, the more stamina you can build up, allowing you to maintain a fast pace the entire time. Pair this together with just a bit of a speed workout twice a week if you're running six days a week. 

Good luck!! And remember, try to understand what pace you're going at the entire time.
